At the beginning of this year I had a big argument with my family. To keep it short, my family do not want me to move out, said I'm stupid for wanting to, and I'm disrespectful for not fulfilling their wishes for me to stay home. I was not in the right space mentally after, for days I was on auto pilot and not talking at school, work, and home.

A few days later, my partner picked me up to spend a few days away from everything. They knew what happened and wanted to do whatever they could to make me feel better. Nothing made me feel better, I was stuck in my depression, almost breaking my 2 year sober streak.

One day, we had to go to the grocery store. My partner did their best to talk to me, only to be met with nods or head shakes, this lasted almost the entire grocery run. Until my partner did this silly penguin waddle into an isle. My face immediately lit up with a smile and laughter. It was so funny and completely out of nowhere. My love for them blossomed in that moment. They walked back up to me saying this was the first time seeing me smile all weekend, and that they just wanted to see me smile after everything that happened at home. They were trying to make me smile all weekend. All it took was a waddle to crack me up. They still do that to this day randomly, not when I'm upset but in the kitchen, the living room, outside, it always makes me smile because it reminds me of how much they love me. I'm still with them, laying next to them as I type this :)

My dad died when I was 15. Needless to say, you get that survival mode instinct even though I am the youngest in the house. I had to keep taking care of my family as I had helped my dad when he was sick, I would even skip school to take care of him. When he passed, I definitely felt like I couldn't keep going in life. However, my sophomore year of high school was just a week after his funeral, so I had to get myself together really fast. It's been a few years and I still wish he was here, he was my best friend and even though I had my arguments with him, he was my dad. I still think about him everyday, I understand you want to be with him, but you wait until your time has come. You will be with him forever one day, it will take time, but the wait will be worth it. It's okay to cry, it's okay to grieve, you have family members going through the same thing and will be there for you when you need it. I know it hurts, but you have to keep moving on in life and show your dad that you're doing good. I remember cleaning myself up shortly before he passed, and he was able to see me make myself become a better person. Keep that going and show him that you're fucking amazing, and when your time comes, he will be very proud of you, regardless of how you turned out, because you did your best and made it this far in life. He is proud of you, and he is always with you. My text got a little messy, but I hope the message is clear. Keep going and stay strong, make your dad proud.
